name: @cloudsforge/mint
description: Token creation. Orders, a token registry, contracts compiled to committed bytecode, and a deploy that leaves the HTTP request: POST /tokens/:id/deploy answers 202 with a status URL and the chain work runs as a leased job.

scripts._test: --test-concurrency=1 is required, not a preference: every database test file truncates this service's tables between cases, and node:test runs FILES in parallel by default. A TRUNCATE takes an AccessExclusiveLock, so one file's reset deadlocks against another file's inserts (40P01). Cases within a file already run in order.
scripts._compile:contracts: Regenerates the COMMITTED artefact src/contracts/generated.ts. CI reruns it and fails on any diff, which is what stops the bytecode this service deploys drifting from the source a reviewer read. The solc and @openzeppelin/contracts versions are EXACT-pinned for exactly that reason.

_localDependencies: Every sibling takes 'link:', not 'file:'. A 'file:' path PACKS the dependency, and each of
these packages declares files: ['dist'] with a publishConfig that points main/types at dist/.
Packing therefore installs a package whose exports resolve to a dist/ that has not been built,
while its 'main' in the working tree still says src/index.ts. 'link:' symlinks the checkout in
place, so the working-tree manifest is the one that is read and the package keeps using its own
already-installed node_modules — which is also what a 'workspace:^' transitive needs.
@cloudsforge/contracts-chain is EXACT-PINNED, never caret-ranged. This service and custody must
agree byte-for-byte about a chain id: a skew there is not a 500, it is a contract creation bound
to the wrong network and broadcastable on a chain the customer never asked to deploy on.
There is no chain library here — no ethers, no @solana/web3.js. This service builds ONE EVM
transaction shape (a legacy zero-value contract creation) and hands it to custody as a JSON
object; custody is the only place a private key exists and therefore the only place a serialiser
is needed. What is left is keccak256, for EIP-55, for the transaction id and for the CREATE
address derivation, and that is a permutation table rather than a dependency on the one path
where a wrong answer deploys a customer's contract to an address nobody can find.
